record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: In a porous body with a free surface, how should the free-boundary problem for seepage of fluid out of the porous body be formulated and analyzed within the homogenization framework for solid-fluid mixtures?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a porous body occupying a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2,3$) modeled as a solid–fluid mixture with a periodic microstructure of period $\varepsilon$: at the microscale, $\Omega$ is decomposed into a solid skeleton $\Omega_s^\varepsilon$ and a connected fluid-filled pore network $\Omega_f^\varepsilon$, with the fluid governed by the (incompressible) Stokes equations in $\Omega_f^\varepsilon$ and the solid by linear elasticity in $\Omega_s^\varepsilon$, coupled by the usual continuity of velocity and traction on the solid–fluid interface.

Assume that a portion $\Gamma \subset \partial\Omega$ of the boundary is exposed to the exterior (e.g., to air at atmospheric pressure), so that the fluid may seep out of the body through $\Gamma$. The wetted part $\Gamma^+ \subset \Gamma$ (where fluid actually exits) and the dry part $\Gamma^0 = \Gamma \setminus \Gamma^+$ are not prescribed a priori; their common boundary inside $\Gamma$ is a free boundary to be determined as part of the solution, subject to:
- on $\Gamma^+$: the fluid pressure equals the external (atmospheric) pressure and fluid exits with non-negative normal flux;
- on $\Gamma^0$: the normal fluid flux vanishes and the pressure is below atmospheric.

Problem. Formulate, within the framework of homogenization of solid–fluid mixtures, the free-boundary problem for seepage of fluid out of $\Omega$ through $\Gamma$. Specifically:

(a) Derive, as $\varepsilon \to 0$, the macroscopic (homogenized) system of equations governing the effective fluid pressure, fluid velocity (Darcy-type), and solid displacement on $\Omega$, together with the effective Signorini-type complementarity conditions on $\Gamma$ that characterize the free boundary separating $\Gamma^+$ from $\Gamma^0$.

(b) Establish existence (and, where possible, uniqueness and regularity) of solutions to the resulting homogenized free-boundary problem, and prove rigorous convergence of solutions of the $\varepsilon$-problems to solutions of the homogenized free-boundary problem.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches reveal extensive work on homogenization of fluid flow in porous media, on Beavers–Joseph-type interface conditions between free fluid and porous regions, and on classical free-boundary seepage problems (e.g., the rectangular dam). However, no source directly formulating and rigorously analyzing the seepage free-boundary problem within the homogenization framework for coupled solid–fluid mixtures was found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Higher order homogenized boundary conditions for flows over rough and porous surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Derives homogenized macroscopic models with unconfined free flow (Navier–Stokes) and seepage (Darcy) inside the porous domain.
status_evidence.claim: Related homogenization results exist for porous/free-fluid interfaces but do not address the seepage free-boundary problem for solid–fluid mixtures.

status_evidence.title: A free boundary problem for fluid flow through porous media
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the free boundary problem of steady seepage through a rectangular dam without invoking homogenization of a solid–fluid mixture.
status_evidence.claim: Classical seepage free-boundary problems are studied outside the homogenization-of-mixtures framework.

status_evidence.title: Theoretical formulation and computational aspects of a two-scale homogenization scheme for poro-elastic fluid-saturated porous media
status_evidence.snippet: Two-scale homogenization for poro-elastic fluid-saturated media, without treating a seepage free boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Homogenization frameworks for solid–fluid mixtures exist but do not incorporate the seepage free-boundary problem.
